title: Import | Export
description: Bring data in from a spreadsheet, or take it out. You review every row before anything is saved.

import.title: Import
import.hint: Data in another app or file? Download the template for what you want to import, copy your data into it, then upload it. Files you exported here earlier can be uploaded as they are.
import.step1Hint: The template lists the columns and what to enter in each.

exportAll.title: Export
exportAll.hint: Take your data out, to keep, edit or use elsewhere.
exportAll.sheetHint: The same columns as the import template, plus an id. Edit it and upload it again to update your data. A full copy of everything is a backup (Settings).

template.intro: Fill in one row per item on the first sheet, then upload the file on the Import page.
template.required: Columns marked with * are required. Leave a cell empty to keep what you already have.
template.multicolor: A multicolor print uses one Spool, Filament and Filament used (g) per color: the first set, then Spool 2 and so on, up to 16.
template.trackUsage: Track usage: leave empty or enter yes to subtract the filament from your spools. Enter no to save the print and its filament without changing your spools' weights.
template.costs: Count in costs, Lifetime (hours) and Include maintenance: leave empty on a new row to use the defaults from Costs settings.
template.clientMatch: A client is found by its Mobile, else its Email, else its VAT number. A new Mobile, Email or VAT number can't be one another client has.
template.quoteCost: A quote here is a typed-in print: Unit cost is what one print costs to make. Leave Quantity, Labor and the percentages empty on a new quote to use the defaults from Costs settings. Client and Project must already exist.
template.orderProjects: Client, Quote and Project must already exist. Name several projects in the Project cell separated by ; (for example 1-Box; 2-Lid). Status is one of your order statuses, empty on a new order is the first one.
template.maintenanceTypes: Target is printer or accessory. Every and Warn before are in days, hours (Every may have decimals) and prints; leave one empty to not use it. Warn alert and Due alert: yes or no, empty uses the maintenance settings. Models (for example Bambu Lab X1C), Printers and Accessories are lists separated by ;. Models, printers and accessories must already exist. Accessory types are free text. Leave them all empty for every printer or accessory.
template.maintenance: One row per maintenance done. Type, and the Printer or Accessory it was done on, must already exist; give the one the type is for. Done is the date and time (for example 2026-03-01 14:30). Runtime at and Prints at: leave empty to use what the printer or accessory had at that time.
template.orderLinks: One row per project of an order. The Order is its number and the Project its number or name; both must already exist. Moving a row to another project is refused while the order has prints of the project it leaves.
template.accessoryInstalls: One row per period an accessory is on a printer. Accessory and Printer must already exist, by number or name (for example 1-AMS). Leave Removed empty if it is still on the printer. An accessory can't be on two printers at once.
template.projects: A row with a Number updates that project. Folder is the full path of the project's folder inside one of your project folders (Settings); leave it empty to pick or create one in the review. A folder can belong to one project only. Prints are linked to each project after the import, the same way a folder scan links them, and you can change them in the review.
template.error: Couldn't build the template. Is the server running?
template.catalogRefs: Brands, printer models and filament materials must already exist: import them first, or add them in the catalog.
template.modelPicture: Picture shows "yes" when a model has a picture. It is for information only: leave it as it is or empty. A file can't add a picture; add one on the model's page, or import the model from a slicer, which fills a missing picture.

hints.ref: A name. Pick one from the list or type a new one; new names are added for you.
hints.money: An amount in your currency, e.g. 19.99.
hints.color: A colour as a hex code, e.g. #ff8800.
hints.datetime: A date and time, as YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (UTC unless you add an offset like +01:00).

upload.hint: An .xlsx (the template), a .csv whose first row holds the column names, or a .json list of objects named like the columns. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
upload.error: Couldn't read that file. Use the template, a CSV whose first row holds the column names, or a JSON list.

errors.not_a_datetime: Not a date and time (use YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM)
errors.unresolved: Not found, or matches more than one
errors.not_opened: This spool was opened after the print started
errors.overlap: The accessory is on a printer during that period
errors.wrong_target: Give one printer or accessory, the one this type is for
errors.outside_roots: Not inside one of your project folders
errors.folder_in_use: Another project, or an earlier row, has this folder

missing.filamentBrands: Brands you don't have yet, added when their rows are imported: {{names, list}}.
missing.filamentMaterials: Materials you don't have yet, added when their rows are imported: {{names, list}}.
missing.filamentProfiles: Filament profiles you don't have yet, added when their rows are imported: {{names, list}}.
missing.brands: Printer brands you don't have yet, added when their rows are imported: {{names, list}}.
missing.printerModels: Printer models you don't have yet, added when their rows are imported: {{names, list}}.
missing.projects: Projects you don't have yet, added without a folder when their rows are imported: {{names, list}}.

review.title: Review rows
review.emptyBody: The file has a header row but nothing below it.
review.duplicateTarget: Picked for more than one row
review.confirmBody: A backup is taken first. If any row fails, nothing is imported.
review.error: Couldn't import, so nothing was changed.
review.needsProject: Pick a project, or No project
review.noSpool: No spool: the grams wait for review
review.checkSpool: Picked from several spools of this colour: check it
review.trackUsageFor: Take the filament of row {{row}} from the spools
review.fixCells: Fix the cells marked in red

done.summary: Import finished: {{created, number}} created, {{updated, number}} updated.

projects.toCreateNamed: New folder, named by number and name
projects.createBody: The folder is made when you import. Leave the name empty to name it by the project's number and name, like 012_Vase.
projects.fromFolder: Take the name, description and link from the folder
projects.printsBody: These prints get this project. The list starts with the ones it has and the ones linked by name, the same way a folder scan links them.

source.description: Review what this source offers. Nothing is saved until you confirm.
source.error: Couldn't read this from the integration. Check that it is connected and set up in Integrations.
source.emptyBody: The source has nothing of this type, or nothing you don't already have.

zip.cardTitle: Printer and filament profiles from a slicer
zip.cardHint: Running on a server with no slicer installed? Zip your slicer's config folder on the PC that has it and import its brands, printers and filament profiles from the zip.
zip.title: Import from a slicer zip
zip.description: Zip your slicer's config folder on the PC that has it, upload it here and review what it offers. Nothing is saved until you confirm.

steps.open: On the PC where {{name}} is installed, open its config folder: Help → Show Configuration Folder.
steps.windows: Windows: {{folder}} (paste it into the File Explorer address bar)
steps.select: Select the system and user folders. The rest (cache, logs, plugins) isn't needed.
steps.zip: Zip them: Windows – right-click → Send to → Compressed (zipped) folder; macOS – right-click → Compress; Linux – run zip -r slicer.zip system user in that folder.

zip.none: No slicer here can read a catalog from a zip.
zip.expired: This upload is gone. Upload the zip again.

errors.invalid_zip: Couldn't read this file as a zip.
errors.not_slicer_folder: This zip doesn't look like a slicer config folder. It needs the system and/or user folders in it.
errors.zip_too_large: This zip is too large. Zip only the system and user folders.
errors.error: Couldn't upload the zip. Is the server running, and is the file under 100 MB?
